ideas.truth: Midday heat makes you crave a jolt of cold before you crave the taste.
ideas.moment: The exact second the cap cracks and condensation mists out.
ideas.key_frame: Macro on the cap twisting open, a fine cold mist puffing into frame.

ideas.truth: The fridge is the modern icebox of relief — you don't drink cold coffee, you rescue yourself with it.
ideas.moment: The bottle emerging from fridge frost into light.
ideas.key_frame: Fridge-door glow, bottle silhouette fogged then clearing to reveal the label.

ideas.truth: Refreshment is judged by the eyes before the tongue — condensation, ice, and a clean dark pour say cold faster than any word.
ideas.moment: The pour hitting ice, the exact instant heat visibly loses.
ideas.key_frame: Dark cold brew cascading over ice in extreme slow motion, bottle and glass both in frame.

why: It gives Veo one literal physical action per scene (droplet fall, then pour), needs zero human presence to read as chilled and fresh, and gives the label two clean, code-free moments to stay legible on a phone.
treatment: We open tight: a bead of condensation is already mid-slide down the dark glass of a Kaapi Cold bottle, resting on wet black stone under a cool teal backlight. It gathers speed, joins smaller droplets, and settles at the label's edge as ice cubes shimmer, soft-focus, in the foreground. Ambient chill hum, the faint click of ice. Hard cut: the bottle, tilted from off-frame, pours an unbroken stream of dark cold brew into a glass packed with ice. The liquid swirls, rises, and settles as the last drop falls and ripples calm. No hands, no faces — only bottle, glass, stone, and cold light throughout. The film ends holding still on the full glass beside the standing bottle, label sharp and legible, condensation beaded on both. Text confirms the name and the promise. Sound cuts to silence on the final frame.

scenes.prompt: Extreme macro shot, camera slowly pushing in on rails, shallow depth of field. A single droplet of condensation on the dark glass bottle breaks loose and slides slowly down the surface, gathering smaller droplets as it falls until it settles at the edge of the black label; in the soft-focus foreground, ice cubes catch cool light and shift slightly. The setting is a wet dark stone surface under a cool teal backlight with faint chill mist drifting through frame. The mood is quiet, cinematic and refreshing, still except for the droplet's fall. Ambient sound of soft ice clinking and a low chilled hum fills the silence.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: A 250 ml cylindrical glass bottle of cold brew coffee, three quarters full of dark liquid, wrapped in a matte black label with a small kraft-paper tag tied to the neck with twine and a black screw cap. The glass beads with fine condensation, standing on wet dark stone, a matching dark backdrop close behind so reflection fills the curve. Extreme macro framing, dim glass-edge highlight, cool teal backlight, one droplet frozen mid-slide, soft-focus ice cubes in the foreground.
scenes.S1_feeling: A held breath of cool relief before anything happens.
scenes.S2_first_frame: Extreme macro, mid-action — the droplet is already sliding, not forming; ice cubes soft-focus in front; bottle label just visible at frame edge.
scenes.S3_one_action: One condensation droplet slides down the glass, gathering smaller droplets, and comes to rest at the label's edge — the full 8 seconds.
scenes.S4_new_information: We learn the product is cold, glass, and branded — nothing else has been shown yet, so this scene carries the whole introduction.
scenes.S5_impact: A quiet payoff that reads as genuinely cold even on mute — a single clean motion, big enough to land on a phone screen.

scenes.prompt: Slow-motion tracking shot at eye level with the glass, camera holding steady then drifting a few inches to follow the pour. Dark cold brew coffee pours in an unbroken stream from the tilted bottle's spout into a glass packed with ice, only the bottle and glass occupying the frame throughout. The liquid cascades down, swirls around the ice, and rises to fill the glass, ending as the last drop falls and ripples settle. The setting is the same wet dark stone surface with cool teal-blue ambient light and a soft rim light along the bottle's edge. Sound of coffee pouring and ice clinking fills the quiet, ending on a still, sharp frame of the full glass beside the bottle.
scenes.first_frame_still_prompt: A 250 ml cylindrical glass bottle of cold brew coffee, three quarters full of dark liquid, wrapped in a matte black label with a kraft-paper neck tag and black screw cap, beaded with condensation, standing on wet dark stone before a close matching backdrop. The bottle alone tilts into frame, a stream of dark coffee already leaving the spout mid-air toward a glass of ice below, cool teal-blue ambient light, soft rim light along the bottle's edge.
scenes.S1_feeling: Release — the heat of the day visibly losing.
scenes.S2_first_frame: The bottle mid-pour with no hand visible, the stream already leaving the spout, glass of ice waiting below.
scenes.S3_one_action: The stream falls, swirls through the ice, fills the glass, and the last drop lands with a ripple that settles — the full 7 seconds.
scenes.S4_new_information: We learn how it's meant to be drunk and see the full bottle-and-glass pairing for the first time; we cut here right as the droplet scene has made its point.
scenes.S5_impact: The film's biggest visual payoff — dark liquid over ice is the clearest possible 'chilled and fresh' image, held still at the end so the product can be read even silent.

finish.copy_placement: On-screen text supers added by code: 'Kaapi Cold' appears low-third around 1s into Scene 1; 'Cold brew. Always fresh.' appears in the final 2 seconds of Scene 2, high-contrast white with a thick dark outline measured against the darkest patch of stone/liquid.
finish.end_card: Final held frame of Scene 2 (full glass beside the standing bottle) becomes the end card, with the Kaapi Cold logo lockup and tagline placed beneath the product, sound cut to silence.
finish.music: Minimal cool downtempo lo-fi bed, mostly texture — kept low so the ice-clink and pour sounds stay foregrounded.

decisions.D1_idea: The exact moment cold brew hits ice and the day's heat visibly loses — the pour is the payoff.
decisions.D2_conflict: Midday heat in an Indian city makes hot or sugary drinks unappealing to an urban professional scrolling Reels on a work break; the specific worry is that iced coffee will taste watered-down or fake — the tension is wanting a cold caffeine hit that still feels crafted, not a diluted substitute.
decisions.D3_roles: The customer is an urban professional in their late-20s to mid-30s, reaching for relief from afternoon heat and fatigue, never shown on screen per the brief; Kaapi Cold is both hero and guide — the bottle stands in for the buyer's craving and performs its own resolution on screen.
decisions.D4_opening: First 2 seconds: extreme macro close-up, mid-action — a condensation droplet already sliding down the glass, not starting to form. This is the visual surprise that hooks.
decisions.D5_brand: The bottle and its label (reading 'KAAPI COLD' directly on the glass, not just via text supers) are visible from second 0; label is legible by roughly 3s into Scene 1; the product recurs physically through both scenes and again as the hero pairing (bottle + full glass) in the closing freeze frame; brand name is additionally reinforced via on-screen text supers at ~1s and on the end card, with no spoken name used.
decisions.D6_ask_and_end: Implicit ask — try it cold, right now — carried entirely by picture (bottle and full glass side by side) and the closing text super, no hard voice CTA. Final frame: bottle and full glass in sharp focus, product filling most of the frame, per default of ending on the product.

D7_product_truth.fact: It is a cold brew coffee
Packaged in a 250 ml glass bottle
Label design (matte black label printed with 'KAAPI COLD' in white sans-serif type, kraft-paper neck tag, black cap) is a director's invention since no photo was supplied
D7_product_truth.source: invented — no photo supplied, kept identical word-for-word across both scenes

D7_product_truth.fact: On-screen tagline 'Cold brew. Always fresh.' is a creative translation of the customer's request to 'make it feel chilled and fresh' into a closing line — it is not a confirmed product claim (e.g. shelf life, no-preservative status)
D7_product_truth.source: derived from customer's own words; flagged for customer sign-off before this specific wording airs

decisions.D8_deviations: No spoken brand line or voiceover was added, even though Ogilvy's device is to use the brand name within the first 10 seconds aloud, because the customer explicitly said 'no people' and wanted a pure ambient product feel for Reels; brand presence is instead carried by the physical label plus on-screen text supers. The 15s runtime was split into an 8s and a 7s Veo scene, joined by a hard cut at the pour, since Veo generates in fixed 8-second units.
